messages.subject: Generating a log file
parts:
Hello shiny community.
I'm having some troubles finishing a big application.
I am currently trying to export some log file as in sas. I would basically want to export a file where I could find all the code executed during the app, all the warnings/errors generated and, if it's possible, the names of the object generated at the moment they are generated (I'm not sure I'm very clean on this one).
I tried kind of all the solutions I found about debugging an app (cat, browser etc), but it's not really what I am expecting.

Do you know any solution that could help me ?!

Thank you in advance for your help.

Pauline

messages.author: a417fa537bba98f2
messages.subject: Re: Generating a log file
parts:
Hi,

I am definitely not an advanced shiny user but I have sort of a similar goal as I try to keep track of user interactions with the app.

You have probably already tried these, but just in case:

First thing that came to mind was to add some commands at the end of each function that would append a summary line of the call (timestamp + functionName + arg 1 + arg 2 + ...) to an R object. So far I use this approach as it suits my purpose well enough but there are probably better ways, like defining a function that could take each of your functions as an argument and do both the call and the log update. Maybe there are also subtleties to be taken into account depending on what you plan to do with your logs (like re-run the commands)

Looking around I also found out about the log4r package that should help with the warnings/errors.

I too indeed remain curious of other/better ways to log what is going during a shiny session (ui-wise and server-wise) but I hope this helps a bit.

Best,
Bastien
